newsitem.title: USA: Cochran lawyers see no legal basis for US appeal.
newsitem.headline: Cochran lawyers see no legal basis for US appeal.

text.p: Lawyers for former Oklahoma bond dealer Robert Cochran said on Wednesday that they see no legal basis for a U.S. appeal of a recent major ruling in their client's favor.
"We don't see a legal basis to petition for rehearing," Cochran lawyer Drew Neville told Reuters by telephone.

Reuters reported May 6 that the U.S. government is expected to ask the full U.S. Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals to rehear part of a March 27 ruling that reversed last year's criminal conviction of Cochran on wire fraud charges.

A three-member panel of the Tenth Circuit on March 27 unanimously reversed a federal jury conviction of Cochran on eight charges of wire fraud and money laundering in connection with bonds issued by two Midwest bond authorities.
The U.S. Justice Department's appellate division is expected to appeal the reversal, a source told Reuters on Tuesday.
"It's expected that the appellate section will file a petition for rehearing on Thursday," the source said.

The source said Justice will ask the court to rehear that part of the decision dealing with Oklahoma City Airport Trust bonds, which were taxable. Justice will not ask for a new ruling concerning Sisters of St. Mary Healthcare System of St. Louis bonds, which were tax-exempt, the source said.

"I'm not surprised that they are going to petition for rehearing because of the publicity attendant to the case," Neville said. "For whatever reason, the government has chosen to proceed on a very, very novel (path)," Neville said. "There is no legal support for the government's decision in this case," he added.

The three-member panel ruled in March that Cochran did not have to disclose outside fees he got in connection with the two bond offerings because he was not acting in an official capacity with the issuers and, therefore, had no duty to disclose.
